tool-cloakbrowser.title: CloakBrowser: a Chromium drop-in for Playwright with C++-level fingerprint patches
tool-cloakbrowser.note: A custom Chromium build that drops straight into Playwright, 87 C++-level patches, with humanize and proxy support. Wrapper code is MIT, the binary needs a license key.

sections.t: Automated browser keeps getting flagged as a bot? Patch it at Chromium's C++ core
sections.lead: CloakBrowser is a custom Chromium build that drops straight into Playwright, with Puppeteer support. Fingerprints are patched in the C++ source instead of injected JavaScript, so you only change the browser launch code.
ticks: 87 fingerprint patches at the C++ level
A Playwright drop-in with humanize and proxy
MIT wrapper, the binary needs a license key

sections.t: Use responsibly: this is a browser that spoofs device identity for automation. Only use it on your own sites, on public data you're allowed to collect, or with permission. Automation that breaks terms of service (especially on Facebook, Zalo, TikTok...) can get accounts banned and may be illegal. CloakBrowser's README also explicitly forbids unauthorized automation, credential stuffing and abusive account creation.
What CloakBrowser does for you

items.d: Fingerprints are patched in Chromium's C++ source, not via JavaScript injection or config flags. The binary's Ed25519 signature is verified before extraction.
humanize=True: Bézier-curve mouse movement, typing with random delays, natural-paced scrolling.

HTTP and SOCKS5 proxy support, geoip=True to match timezone and language to the proxy IP, WebRTC IP spoofing. Persistent profiles keep cookies and localStorage between runs, and Chrome extensions can be loaded. Poses as Windows by default on Linux and Windows, with an optional macOS identity.

items.t: Switch from Playwright in one place
items.d: launch() returns a Playwright Browser object, so new_page(), close()... work as usual. There's also cloakserve to run the browser as a CDP server, a Docker image, a .NET client and a CLI (install binary, diagnostics, cache management).

sections.t: See it in action: input → process → output
Testing your own landing page with CloakBrowser instead of Playwright

input.label: Your code (test_landing.py)
input.t:
from cloakbrowser import launch
browser = launch(humanize=True)
page = browser.new_page(); page.goto("https://shop-cua-ban.vn")
page.screenshot(path="landing.png"); browser.close()

steps: The first run downloads the roughly 200 MB Chromium binary and caches it.
The key is read from the CLOAKBROWSER_LICENSE_KEY environment variable before launch.
launch() returns a Playwright Browser and opens the page with human-like mouse and scrolling.
The rest runs like normal Playwright: take a screenshot, then close.

output.label: Terminal
output.t:
$ export CLOAKBROWSER_LICENSE_KEY=...   # your key, never in code
$ python test_landing.py
Downloading Chromium binary (first run, about 200 MB)...
Ed25519 signature verified, extracted to cache
Launching: Chromium 156.0.8078.47.1, Windows identity
Opening https://shop-cua-ban.vn ... 200 OK
Page title: Shop Của Bạn | November deals
Saved landing.png (1366 x 768)
Browser closed.

sections.note: Illustrative example, real logs may differ. Needs a license key (free tier: one session); use only on your own site or with permission.

sections.t: Info taken from the repo's GitHub page, read on 4/11/2026. Stars, versions and terms may have changed, and the claims about passing bot checks come from the author; I haven't verified them independently.
Quick comparison with Camoufox

head: Criteria
CloakBrowser
Camoufox
rows: MIT wrapper, binary needs a license key
Free tier limited to one concurrent session, Pro plan available
Linux, Windows, macOS, doesn't run on WSL
Under development, may not be stable for production

sections.t: My take: if you need Chromium, want a supported prebuilt binary and are fine with a license key, look at CloakBrowser. If you need fully open source with no key, and can accept the Firefox engine and the 'not stable for production' note, look at Camoufox. Either way, test it on your own use case.
Repo info

head: Item
Details
rows: A custom Chromium build, a drop-in replacement for Playwright (Puppeteer supported)
Linux x86_64 and arm64, macOS arm64 and x86_64, Windows x86_64
About 32.7k stars, 2.7k forks, 137 open issues, 390 commits
Wrapper code (Python, JS, .NET): MIT. Chromium binary: separate license, needs a license key
README says 'Last tested: Nov 2026' and describes itself as maintained

sections.t: Installation

pip install cloakbrowser

npm install cloakbrowser playwright-core   # or puppeteer-core

dotnet add package CloakBrowser

items: The ~200 MB binary downloads automatically on first run and is cached. No need to run playwright install chromium, but you still need the system libraries Playwright requires.
launch() returns a Playwright Browser object, so new_page(), close()... work as usual. Switching from Playwright only means changing the browser launch code.

sections.t: License and license key (important)

head: Plan
Terms
rows: Sign up with email to get a key, one concurrent session. Always gets the latest build
More concurrent sessions, can pin a Chromium version to roll back
Personal and commercial per the README, no redistributing the binary. Serving third parties needs an OEM or SaaS license

items: Every launch needs the key, set via the CLOAKBROWSER_LICENSE_KEY environment variable. Don't put the key in source code or chats.
The keyless v146 binary is only in the old wrapper (pip install "cloakbrowser<0.7") and no longer gets updates.
Full terms are in the repo's BINARY-LICENSE.md; read it before commercial use.

sections.t: Limitations the README admits

items: It doesn't solve CAPTCHAs, it tries to keep them from appearing. No built-in proxy rotation; you bring your own proxies.
Some sites still detect headless mode; running headed is recommended (use Xvfb on Linux).
On Linux, a convincing Windows identity needs real Windows fonts installed, and a macOS identity needs real Mac fonts.
Puppeteer can be detected by reCAPTCHA Enterprise, so Playwright is recommended. page.wait_for_timeout() and page.evaluate() may send CDP commands some systems can spot.
Playwright's context.request and route.fetch() don't go through SOCKS5 or authenticated proxies.
The README admits detection may catch up in the future; it's an ongoing arms race.

sections.t: Ideas for using it in the Library

items: Test your own website and landing pages across many browser setups and regions.
Run browser agents on a VPS (pairs with the OVH VPS for Hermes Agent guide) to get blocked by mistake less often when accessing public data you're allowed to use.
Study how anti-bot systems work, in your own environment.

sections.t: Install safety notes

items: There are many forks and look-alikes (such as zapabob, DivMode, dgtlmoon, Munasco) with different numbers. Only use the official CloakHQ/CloakBrowser repo and the author's own PyPI or npm packages.
The prebuilt binary is downloaded from the publisher, so run it in an isolated environment (a separate VPS or Docker), away from API keys, passwords or important data.

sections.t: Link
FAQ

items.q: Does CloakBrowser solve CAPTCHAs?
items.a: No. It tries to keep CAPTCHAs from appearing rather than solving them. It also has no built-in proxy rotation; you bring your own proxies.

items.q: Can I use it for free?
items.a: There's a free tier: sign up with email to get a key, one concurrent session. The paid Pro plan gives more sessions and lets you pin a Chromium version. The keyless v146 binary is only in the old wrapper and no longer gets updates.

items.q: Can I use it commercially or for clients?
items.a: The README allows personal and commercial use, but no redistributing the binary. Serving third parties needs an OEM or SaaS license. Read BINARY-LICENSE.md before commercial use.

items.q: Is it fine for automation on Facebook, Zalo or TikTok?
items.a: No. Automation that breaks terms of service can get accounts banned and may be illegal. The README also forbids unauthorized automation, credential stuffing and abusive account creation.

items.q: Is it guaranteed to beat every anti-bot system?
items.a: Nothing is guaranteed. The claims about passing bot checks come from the author and I haven't verified them independently, and the README admits detection may catch up in the future.

sections.t: A Chromium that's hard to spot, worth trying when used in the right place
sections.d: Install with pip, npm or dotnet, set the key via the CLOAKBROWSER_LICENSE_KEY environment variable, change the browser launch code and you're running. Test it on your own use case before relying on it.
sections.note: Only use it on your own sites, on public data you're allowed to collect, or with permission. Install only from the official CloakHQ/CloakBrowser repo and run it in an isolated environment.

tool-camoufox.title: Camoufox: open-source anti-detect Firefox for scraping and AI agents
tool-camoufox.note: A Firefox build that spoofs fingerprints, driven by Playwright, with humanize, geoip and proxy. Browser MPL-2.0, packages MIT. Under development.

sections.t: A Firefox that changes its device identity, driven by Playwright
sections.lead: Camoufox is an open-source anti-detect Firefox build for web scraping and AI agents. Each launch gets a consistent device identity, and the automation code runs where the page can't see it. The project is still under development and not yet suited to stable production use.
ticks: Fingerprints spoofed from real-world device distributions
Use it like regular Playwright, in Python or Node.js
Browser MPL-2.0, Python and TypeScript packages MIT

sections.t: Use responsibly: this is a browser that spoofs device identity for automation. Only use it on your own sites, on public data you're allowed to collect, or with permission. Automation that breaks terms of service (especially on Facebook, Zalo, TikTok...) can get accounts banned and may be illegal.

Info taken from the repo's GitHub page, read on 4/11/2026. Stars, versions and terms may have changed, and the claims about passing bot checks come from the author; I haven't verified them independently.
What the tool does for you

items.d: Each launch gets a consistent device identity, generated from real-world device distributions. Need several identities? Open several contexts in one browser via NewContext().
Navigator, screen, WebGL, WebGPU, fonts, audio, voices, media devices, timezone, locale, geolocation and WebRTC IP are all spoofed.

items.t: Human-like input, location that matches the proxy
items.d: humanize=True gives human-like mouse movement, based on recordings of real interactions. Use a proxy with geoip=True so timezone, language, location and WebRTC IP match the exit IP.

items.t: Lean, and the page can't see the controls
items.d: Ships with uBlock Origin, with telemetry and extras stripped out. Playwright uses Firefox's built-in Juggler protocol, and the automation code runs in an isolated world.

sections.t: See it in action: input → process → output
Checking how your own landing page looks to visitors in Japan via a proxy

input.label: Your code (check_jp.py)
input.t:
from camoufox.sync_api import Camoufox
with Camoufox(headless=True, proxy={"server": "http://proxy-jp:8080"}, geoip=True) as browser:
    page = browser.new_page(); page.goto("https://shop-cua-ban.vn")
    print(page.title()); page.screenshot(path="jp.png")

steps: You install camoufox[geoip] and run camoufox fetch to download the browser.
Each launch generates one consistent Firefox device identity.
geoip=True matches timezone, language, location and WebRTC IP to the proxy IP.
You use page like normal Playwright: open the page, read the title, take a screenshot.

output.label: Terminal
output.t:
$ pip install -U "camoufox[geoip]"
$ camoufox fetch
Camoufox build downloaded

$ python check_jp.py
Shop Của Bạn | 日本向けページ

$ ls
check_jp.py  jp.png

jp.png: the page shows the Japanese version, prices in yen,
a "Free international shipping" banner at the top.

sections.note: Illustrative example, real results depend on your site and proxy. Project still in development, does not run on WSL; use only on your own site or permitted data.

sections.t: Repo info

head: Item
Details
rows: An open-source anti-detect Firefox build for web scraping and AI agents, driven by Playwright
Playwright uses Firefox's built-in Juggler protocol; automation code runs in an isolated world the page can't see
About 13.0k stars, 1.1k forks, 38 open issues, 14 pull requests, 916 commits
Browser (patches and build): MPL-2.0. Python and TypeScript packages: MIT. Cursory mouse data: LGPLv3 or later
camoufox.com and the READMEs in the repo (python, typescript, docs)
README says: 'This project is under development. It may not be suitable for stable production use.'

sections.t: Install and use

pip install -U "camoufox[geoip]"
camoufox fetch

npm install camoufox playwright-core
npx camoufox fetch

from camoufox.sync_api import Camoufox

with Camoufox(headless=True) as browser:
    page = browser.new_page()
    # use it like regular Playwright
The returned browser is a standard Playwright Browser. In Node.js use const browser = await Camoufox({ headless: true }).
Main options

head: Option
What it does
rows: True, or the max seconds per mouse movement
proxy with geoip=True so timezone, language, location and WebRTC IP match the exit IP
True, or 'virtual' and 'virtual-gpu' (the last two on Linux only)
Set the OS per context via NewContext(browser, os=...)
Turn canvas noise on or off
fingerprint_preset, locale, addons, exclude_addons, pin_cpu_cores, main_world_eval, launch_server()

sections.t: The full list is in the repo's python/README.md.
Operating systems

items: Builds run on Linux; Windows and macOS versions are cross-compiled. Packaged architectures: x86_64, arm64, and i686 (Windows only).
The README states 'WSL does not work', so it can't run on WSL.
WebGPU is only available on Windows and Apple-silicon Macs.

sections.t: Limitations the README admits

items: Camoufox only spoofs Firefox identities. Some systems check SpiderMonkey-specific behavior, so it can't pass as Chromium.
Canvas on an OS different from the real machine returns random data and can give it away. Audio rendering and text width results aren't noised.
Enabling instantAnimations can get the browser detected. Media codecs on Linux depend on the libraries installed on the machine.
The README admits Camoufox can still be detected.

sections.t: Maintenance status to watch

items: One fork says the original maintainer has had health issues since 3/2025. That's from a fork and I haven't verified it; check the original repo's commit and issue history to judge how active it is.
Forks list different base Firefox versions (one says 142, another 146); I haven't confirmed which is the latest in the original repo.
The README has a lot of sponsored ads from proxy and scraping service providers, unrelated to what the project does.

sections.t: Install safety notes

items: There are lots of forks named camoufox. Only install from the original daijro/camoufox repo or the official packages, and check the author before installing from a fork.
Run it in an isolated environment (a separate VPS or Docker), away from API keys, passwords or important data.

sections.t: Link
FAQ

items.q: Is Camoufox guaranteed to get past bot-blocking systems?
items.a: No. The README admits Camoufox can still be detected. The claims about passing bot checks come from the author, and I haven't verified them independently.

items.q: Is it OK to run automation on Facebook, Zalo or TikTok with Camoufox?
items.a: Automation that breaks terms of service can get accounts banned and may be illegal. Only use it on your own sites, on public data you're allowed to collect, or with permission.

items.q: Does it run on Windows or WSL?
items.a: The Windows and macOS builds are cross-compiled from Linux and work. WSL doesn't: the README says 'WSL does not work'. The 'virtual' and 'virtual-gpu' headless modes are Linux only.

items.q: Can it pass as Chrome?
items.a: No. Camoufox only spoofs Firefox identities, and some systems check SpiderMonkey-specific behavior.

items.q: Where should I install it from?
items.a: Only from the original daijro/camoufox repo or the official packages, since there are many forks with the same name. Run it on a separate VPS or in Docker, away from API keys, passwords and important data.

What the LUT does for you

items.t: Turns D-Log M into viewable color
items.d: Converts the flat, washed-out D-Log M image to Rec.709, the color space for regular screens.

sections.t: How to use it (from secondary sources, not checked on DJI's page)

head: Software

rows: Per DJI's LUT guide (a 2018 version written for Resolve 15 and older cameras): copy the file into Color Management's LUT folder, in a DJI subfolder, then click Update Lists (only needed once). From a third-party tutorial: load the LUT in Lumetri Color, under Basic Correction, Input LUT, then fine-tune with curves and color wheels. This is a secondary source; the menu path isn't confirmed

items: A common Resolve approach: put the DJI LUT on the last node, with other grading nodes before it.

skill-brainstorm.title: brainstorm: clarify the problem before you start
skill-brainstorm.note: Interview in batches, answer in short · Read existing data first, no needless questions · Package the brief in 6 sections, deliberately without a solution.

sections.t: Many jobs fail simply because they solved the wrong brief
sections.lead: Handing work to an AI or a teammate with one vague sentence often brings back off-target results and a restart from zero. Instead of rushing in, sharpen your axe first. Measure twice, cut once.
ticks: Interview in batches, answer in short
Read existing data first, no needless questions
Package the brief in 6 sections, deliberately without a solution

sections.t: Turn AI into a sharp interviewer that pins down the right brief

items.t: Interview in batches, answer in short
items.d: The AI asks you in batches of 2-5 questions on the same topic, with context, suggested options and reasons. You only need to type something short like '1: A - 2: yes - 3: up to you'.

items.t: Read existing data first, no needless questions
items.d: Before asking, the AI reads the files, documents and spreadsheets it can reach to understand the context. It does not ask again what a source already answers; any source it cannot open becomes a question for you.

items.t: Package the brief in 6 sections, deliberately without a solution
items.d: The result is condensed into 6 parts: Goal, Current state, Problem, Wishes, Constraints and Out of scope. Keeping these separate and not rushing to a solution stops you from drifting off course during execution.

items.t: Cold review, locked only when you nod
items.d: A reader who has not heard the conversation reviews the brief to find anything still vague: a sub-assistant if your AI can open one, otherwise the AI reviews it itself and tells you so. The brief is locked only when you clearly say "OK"; silence does not count.

sections.t: Clarify any vague problem, at work and in daily life

items.t: A coffee shop owner is thinking about opening a second location
items.before: Worries as thoughts come, unsure whether to put cash flow first or test a new concept. Every talk feels foggy.
items.after: The AI interview clearly separates the goal, the current shop's state and the assumptions to check in practice before looking for a site.

items.t: An online shop owner wants to cut the time spent replying to customers on Zalo
items.before: Plans to buy automation software right away, but is unsure whether customers get stuck at price advice or at closing the order. Risk of wasting money.
items.after: The brief states where customers get stuck, the desired response time, the budget and what is still an assumption to check. With that base, you can decide whether software is needed at all.

items.t: A team lead sees the team constantly overloaded
items.before: Plans to ask for more headcount because of the constant pressure, unsure whether the root cause is skills, process or workload.
items.after: The brief states the current workload, the budget constraint and what is still an assumption to check. The hiring decision rests on a clear picture, not on a feeling.

items.t: A professional plans to ask AI to write a small tool or redo a set of content
items.before: A vague one-line description makes the AI invent random features. The result misses the point and needs repeated fixing.
items.after: A clear 6-section brief is ready to hand to the AI for planning, and it rarely has to come back with questions.

items.t: A family is discussing moving house or changing the child's school
items.before: Everyone has a different opinion and argues. Some worry about money, others about distance, and there is no shared criterion.
items.after: A clear package of the shared goal, the maximum budget and the out-of-scope factors, so the whole family can look for a fitting option together.

You: Help me brainstorm opening a second location.

AI: I'll start with a batch of 3 questions about the Goal:

2. Do you want to keep the current menu style? (Suggestions: Yes / No)
3. When do you expect to start operating? (Suggestions: Within 3 months / 6 months / Up to you)

You: 1: B - 2: yes - 3: up to you

- Goal: Test the new shop model in a different area.

sections.t: Frequently asked questions

items.q: Does this skill also make a detailed execution plan?
items.a: No. This skill only focuses on clarifying the brief and describing the problem accurately. It deliberately does not give a solution or make a plan. Once you have a clear 6-section brief, you can act on it yourself or hand it to the AI to plan next.

items.q: What if I get a question I don't know the answer to?
items.a: Just say 'don't know'. The AI will record it as an assumption or a point to check later. The quality of the brief depends directly on your answers.

items.q: Can the skill be used to come up with lists of new ideas or names?
items.a: No, the skill does not do that. Its job is to turn a vague problem into a clear brief, not to list scattered ideas.

items.q: What if the AI in my app does not support installing zip files?
items.a: Just send the SKILL.md file and assets/brief-template.md into the chat and say 'Follow SKILL.md'. The AI will read the instructions and start the workflow right away.

items.q: How do I update when a new version comes out?
items.a: Just download the new zip file and ask the AI to install it again. The AI will ask you before replacing the old version.

items.q: What are the rules for using and editing this skill?
items.a: You may use and edit the skill for your own work and business. You may share the original unchanged for non-commercial purposes, with credit to the source. No reselling, and no releasing edited versions.

sections.t: Install

items.d: Download the ZIP with the button below and unzip it into a permanent folder (for example D:\lanhmar\drive-ebook-reader).
Open chrome://extensions (Edge: edge://extensions), turn on Developer mode, click Load unpacked and pick the unzipped folder. The extension ID is always bijcnaofiojlemmbghgcljfekdaoghbf.

Click the extension icon → “Pick books from Google Drive”, sign in and select one or more books in the Drive window. They land in your Library and open at once; next time the purple “Read without downloading” button on that book's Drive page opens it directly.

sections.t: How access works: the extension only requests Google's drive.file scope, so it can read exactly the books you pick in the Google Drive window and nothing else. Click “Pick books from Google Drive” once (several at a time is fine); they go into your Library and open directly from then on, including from the purple button on the Drive page. No test-user list, no download to disk.
How it works

items: Signs in with chrome.identity using the drive.file scope: Google grants access only to the files you pick in the Google Picker (hosted at lanhmar.id.vn/drive-picker.html), nothing else; the extension only talks to www.googleapis.com.
PDF.js gets a custom PDFDataRangeTransport: whenever it needs data it sends a Range header to the Drive API and receives 206 Partial Content, 1 MB at a time, with background auto-fetch turned off.
Only pages near the viewport are rendered and far pages are released to save RAM; the top bar shows exactly how much data has been fetched.
Tested with a 24 MB PDF: opening fetched about 3 MB, jumping to page 20 another 4 MB. PDFs whose page dictionaries are scattered through the file may need most of the file on first open.
Reading position, font size and the light/sepia/dark theme are stored in chrome.storage.local on your machine.

tool-agent-stack-theory.title: Plugins, MCP, CLI, Skills, Hooks: kitting out your AI agent (read before installing)
tool-agent-stack-theory.note: An AI agent is only as good as the tools it holds. This card explains Claude Code's 5 kinds of tooling, how they differ, the install commands, what they cost and what to watch out for, plus the list of what I have installed.

sections.t: An AI agent is only as good as the tools it holds
sections.lead: On its own an AI model only reads and writes text. For it to read Gmail, make a Canva design or open a PR on GitHub, you have to give it tools. This card shows you what to add, which command installs it, what it costs and what to watch out for.
ticks: 5 kinds of tooling: Skill, MCP, CLI, Hook, Plugin
Exact install commands in Claude Code
Context cost and safety notes

sections.t: After this card you will

items.t: Tell the 5 kinds of tooling apart
items.d: A Skill is a procedure manual, MCP is a socket that plugs the agent into an app, a CLI is a hand tool run in the terminal, a Hook is a rule that fires on its own, and a Plugin is a ready-made toolbox that packs the others.

items.t: Know when to pick a CLI and when to pick MCP
items.d: If there is a good CLI, let the agent type commands. A web app that needs a login and has no CLI gets a remote MCP. A repeat task with your own process gets a Skill.

items.t: Install with the right command and scope
items.d: The /plugin install command, claude mcp add for remote and local servers, and the 3 scopes local, project and user, so you know who can use it and where the config lives.

items.t: Keep the agent light and safe
items.d: Every plugin and MCP adds tool descriptions to every turn. Install few but the right ones, only from sources you know, and keep tokens out of committed files.

sections.t: One line to remember: a Skill is a procedure manual, MCP is a socket that plugs the agent into an app, a CLI is a hand tool run in the terminal, a Hook is a rule that fires on its own, and a Plugin is a ready-made toolbox that packs the others into one install.
Why install anything?

On its own an AI model only reads and writes text. To become an agent that does real work (read Gmail, create a Canva design, open a PR on GitHub, turn a PDF into text) it has to be connected to tools. Claude Code ships with file read/write, terminal commands and web search; everything else you add in the 5 ways below.
The 5 kinds of tooling

head: Kind
What it is
Example I use
Install with
rows: A folder with a SKILL.md file: instructions for doing one kind of task the right way. Claude loads it only when needed.
brainstorm, plan, reflect (see AI Library > Skills)
Copy into ~/.claude/skills/ or install via a plugin
A program that follows the Model Context Protocol and gives the agent a set of "tools" to work with one app.
Notion, Canva, Gmail, Google Drive, Composio
claude mcp add … or turn on a connector on claude.ai
A command-line program. The agent types commands in the terminal like a person, reads the output and carries on.
Your system package manager (brew, winget, npm, pip…)
A command that runs automatically at a fixed moment: before a tool call, when you send a prompt, when a session starts…
The Composio plugin's hook nudges the agent to use Composio when you name an app
settings.json or bundled in a plugin
A one-time install that bundles any mix of skills, agents, slash commands, hooks and MCP servers.

sections.t: How MCP works

Claude Code is an MCP client. Each MCP server declares a list of tools (for example create_design, search_threads). When you hand over a task, Claude reads the tool names and descriptions and picks the right one to call. There are 2 kinds of server:

items.d: Runs on the provider's servers; you paste a URL and sign in with OAuth in your browser. Examples: Notion, Canva, Zapier. Nothing to install on your machine.

Claude Code starts a program on your machine with npx, uvx or docker. Good for work that needs local files or a local browser, such as Playwright MCP. Needs Node, uv or Docker (see the Runtimes card).

head: Scope
Who can use it
Stored in
rows: Only you, only in the current project
.mcp.json at the project root (committed to git)

sections.t: CLI or MCP: which one?

items: There is a good CLI and you use the terminal (git, gh, gcloud, ffmpeg): just let the agent type commands. It already knows the common ones and adds no context cost per turn.
A web app that needs a login and has no CLI (Canva, Notion, Gmail): use a remote MCP, sign in with OAuth once.
A repeat task with your own process (captions in your brand voice): write a Skill.
You want to share the whole kit with teammates or install it on another machine: package it as a Plugin.
This is how I choose, not a hard rule. Many services offer both, e.g. GitHub has gh (CLI) and the GitHub MCP.

sections.t: Install commands in Claude Code

# Open the plugin browser
/plugin

# Install a plugin from Anthropic's official marketplace
/plugin install github@claude-plugins-official

# Install from another marketplace: add the marketplace first
/plugin marketplace add social-media-skills/skills
/plugin install social-media-skills@social-media-skills
sections.cap: Plugins (typed inside a Claude Code session)

sections.t:
# Remote (HTTP)
claude mcp add --transport http notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp

# Local (stdio): everything after -- is the command that runs the server
claude mcp add playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest

# Available in every project
claude mcp add --scope user --transport http canva https://mcp.canva.com/mcp

claude mcp list        # list servers
claude mcp remove notion

Inside a Claude Code session, type /mcp to see which servers are running and to sign in (OAuth). Connectors you turn on at claude.ai (Customize > Connectors) also show up in Claude Code when you sign in with the same account; you can turn them off per project in /mcp.
The hidden cost: context

Every plugin and MCP server adds tool descriptions to the context of every turn. Install too many and the agent gets slower, burns more tokens and picks the wrong tool more often. A plugin's details page in /plugin has a Context cost entry (cost per turn); claude plugin details <name> gives exact figures. Turn off anything you haven't used in a while.
Safety before you install

items: Plugins and MCP servers can run commands on your machine. Install only from sources you know and read the "Will install" list before you confirm.
Never paste tokens or API keys into files you commit (.mcp.json). Use environment variables, e.g. GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN.
Grant the least access: a GitHub token only for the repos you need, the Gmail connector only on when you need it.
Content the agent reads through MCP (emails, web pages, documents) can hide instructions. For sending, deleting or posting, always have the agent ask you first.
For a project's .mcp.json, Claude Code asks you to approve a server before its first use.

items.t: Claude Code: install and manage plugins

sections.t: FAQ

items.q: How is a Skill different from a Plugin?
items.a: A Skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file that explains how to do one kind of task; Claude loads it only when needed. A Plugin is a one-time install that can hold skills, agents, slash commands, hooks and MCP servers.

items.q: Should I use a remote or a local MCP?
items.a: Remote runs on the provider's servers: paste a URL and sign in with OAuth, nothing to install. Local runs on your machine with npx, uvx or docker, which suits work with local files or a local browser.

items.q: Do connectors turned on at claude.ai work in Claude Code?
items.a: Yes, when you sign in with the same account. To turn one off for a single project, use /mcp.

items.q: Is it a problem to install lots of plugins and MCP servers?
items.a: Yes. Each adds tool descriptions to the context of every turn, so the agent gets slower, burns more tokens and picks the wrong tool more often. Check Context cost in /plugin or run claude plugin details <name>, and turn off what you haven't used in a while.

items.q: Where should tokens and API keys go?
items.a: Never in files you commit, such as .mcp.json. Use environment variables, e.g. GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN, and grant the least access.

sections.t: Install few but the right ones, and the agent stays light and accurate

items.q: How do I scope the token safely?
items.a: Choose a fine-grained token and grant access only to the repos you need. A token with write access is the key to your repos: give it an expiry date and revoke it when unused.

items.q: Where do I keep the token?

items.q: Will the agent merge pull requests on its own?

items.q: I already have the gh CLI. Do I need the GitHub MCP?
items.a: You don't need both for the same task. The MCP suits the web or cloud sessions; gh suits a machine where gh is installed and signed in.

sections.t: It differs from Zapier in how you use it: with Zapier you switch on individual actions in advance; with Composio the agent finds the right tool itself and asks you to connect an app when needed. Good when you don't know ahead which apps you'll need.

skill-coding-agent-standards.title: coding-agent-standards: a rulebook that keeps coding agents disciplined
skill-coding-agent-standards.note: One skill bundling a role, 3 rule sets, 6 sub-skills and 3 workflows for AI that writes code: understand before changing, keep changes small, always verify, never push or delete on its own. Markdown only. Repo by danieldev23.

sections.t: Hand coding work to AI without it spreading edits, pushing on its own or pretending it tested
sections.lead: coding-agent-standards bundles a role, 3 rule sets, 6 sub-skills and 3 workflows into one skill for Claude Code. Claude reads the rules before any coding task, or you call it directly with /coding-agent-standards.
ticks: Understand before changing, keep changes scoped
Always run tests, lint and build before saying done
Never push, delete or deploy without asking

sections.t: What the skill does for you

items.d: The agent reads the related code first; if information is missing it reads more or asks, it doesn't guess. With a vague brief it picks the most reasonable reading, states the assumption and carries on.
No drive-by refactors elsewhere. It runs tests, lint and build before saying done; if there are no tests, it writes at least a basic one.

It says what was done, why and what risks remain, and never pretends to have tested. Pushing to the main branch, deleting files or branches, migrations, deploys and sending email all need your approval first.
3 step-by-step workflows for adding a feature, fixing a bug and preparing a pull request, plus 6 sub-skills: code review, debugging, testing, refactoring, documentation, UI design.

sections.t: See it in action: input → process → output
Having the agent fix a sign-up form bug with the bug-fix workflow

input.label: You type
input.t: The sign-up form says success, but an email with a trailing space isn't saved. Please fix it.

steps: Reproduces the bug by running again with an email that has a trailing space.
Narrows the scope and tests one hypothesis at a time to find the root cause.
Writes a test that catches the bug; it must fail before the fix.
Makes the minimal fix right where the bug is, then reruns tests, lint and build.
Reports the cause, the fix, the files and the tests; does not push on its own.

output.label: Agent report
output.t:
Cause: validateEmail() checks the email before trimming spaces,
so "an@vidu.vn " is silently rejected while the form still says success.

Fix: trim spaces before validating (1 line).
File: src/forms/signup.js

Test: tests/signup.test.js
  ✗ before the fix: saves an email with a trailing space
  ✓ after the fix: 24/24 tests pass
Lint: pass · Build: pass

Nothing else changed. Not pushed, waiting for your OK.

skill-chuan-hoa-van-ban.title: chuan-hoa-van-ban: format documents to Decree 30 standards
skill-chuan-hoa-van-ban.note: 28 formatting rules drawn from Decree 30/2020 · Content stays untouched, only the formatting changes · A built-in checker that self-checks and cross-checks the numbers.

sections.t: Outgoing documents: don't let a nice shirt go out with the buttons misaligned
sections.lead: A quote or official letter can have solid content, but three or four fonts and messy amounts make it look rushed. What a machine does well, a person shouldn't do by hand.
ticks: 28 formatting rules drawn from Decree 30/2020
Content stays untouched, only the formatting changes
A built-in checker that self-checks and cross-checks the numbers

sections.t: Put your document into the right format without losing a single number

items.d: A4 paper, margins of 2 cm top, 2 cm bottom, 3 cm left and 1.5 cm right, Times New Roman font, with the full national title, motto, document number and code, place and date, subject line, signature block and recipients list (Nơi nhận). The rules are drawn from Appendix I of the decree on clerical work.

items.t: Content stays untouched, only the formatting changes
items.d: Item names, unit prices, quantities and terms are kept exactly as they are. The skill only cleans out decorative icons and puts amounts and dates into a single format, with a report that lists every change it made.

items.t: A built-in checker that self-checks and cross-checks the numbers
items.d: The bundled checker verifies paper size, margins, font, page numbers, national title, document number, dates and the recipients list. If you have the original Word file, it compares every number of 1,000 or more between the original and the new version. If a number is missing, the AI must fix it before handing the file over.

items.t: One round of questions, several output formats
items.d: If the document number, date, signer or job title is missing, the AI asks once, with a suggestion for each blank. Type "ok" and the AI uses the suggestions. You get a .docx file, an HTML file to open in Google Docs, and a PDF if your machine has LibreOffice.

sections.t: From office work to everyday life, outgoing documents deserve to look serious

items.t: A salesperson or shop owner is about to send a quote to a customer
items.before: A quote typed in a hurry in a chat, with messy fonts and amounts written as 1,350,000đ in one place and 3tr2 in another, which looks unprofessional.
items.after: The quote table sits neatly in the template, amounts are formatted the same way, and it has a document number and a formal date, so you can send it with confidence.

items.t: A business is preparing documents to submit to a government agency or partner
items.before: Struggling to set the margins, putting the national title and motto in the wrong place, or leaving out the subject line the way their clerks are used to.
items.after: The document is laid out by the 28 rules drawn from Decree 30/2020, in the format the recipient is used to reading.

items.t: HR or admin writes a notice about a holiday break or a change in working hours
items.before: The AI wrote the content, but the document still has decorative asterisks, bullets in a different style on every line, and no document number or recipients list.
items.after: A clean Word file: decorative characters removed, bullets in one style, a full signature block and recipients list, ready to print and pin on the notice board or attach to an email.

items.t: An accountant prepares a payment request or a submission to a partner
items.before: Wasting time checking margins line by line, dates abbreviated like 7/10/26, amounts in different styles, and afraid of missing a number when editing by hand.
items.after: Amounts and dates go into one format. With the original Word file, the checker compares every number of 1,000 or more against the original. The AI checks small numbers and item codes by eye and lists them in the report.

items.t: A parents' association or an apartment building's management board has finished writing a petition or notice
items.before: A document for the school board or building management that is awkwardly laid out, like one long message, and lacks weight.
items.after: The same content now has a title, document number, date, signature block and recipients list in the right format, and looks serious when sent out.

sections.t: How to use it

items.d: Download the zip file, give it to your AI and write: 'Install the skill in this file following the INSTALL.md inside.' (Remember to turn on code execution in the chat app).
Open a new conversation, upload your Word or PDF file or paste the text in, and type: 'Please standardize this quote file.'
Answer the one round of format questions (or just type 'ok'), receive the .docx file with a check report, give it a quick look, then send it with confidence.

sections.t: Frequently asked questions

items.q: Does this skill change the content or the prices on its own?
items.a: Not at all. The skill keeps item names, quantities, unit prices and terms exactly as they are. It only changes presentation, such as the format of amounts and dates, fonts and margin layout.

items.q: Does the skill write new documents or review the legal side of a contract?
items.a: No. The skill does not write new content and does not review the legal content of a contract. It only reformats the document you give it.

items.q: Are private businesses required to follow Decree 30/2020?
items.a: Not required. Decree 30 is mandatory for state agencies and state-owned enterprises. The skill uses it as a yardstick for documents sent outside.

items.q: What kind of AI environment does the skill need?
items.a: It needs an AI that can run Python 3 and write files (an AI working on your computer, or a chat app with code execution turned on). If something is missing, the skill stops and says exactly what, and does not build the file "by hand".

items.q: Is the HTML file opened in Google Docs identical to the Word version?
items.a: Not entirely. The Google Docs version keeps the font, font size and tables, but the margins revert to the default and there are no page numbers. The fully compliant version is the .docx file.

items.q: Is it 100% correct to Decree 30, and does it add a seal?
items.a: The skill does not add a seal, and we do not claim "100% correct". The skill follows 28 formatting rules drawn from Appendix I, plus 4 conventions of our own that are listed in the README. You should reread small numbers, phone numbers and item codes before sending.

items.q: What about a contract signed by two parties?
items.a: The skill builds the header, the body and the Party B signature block. You type the Party A signature block into the empty cell in the left column in Word, and the AI will remind you beforehand. The checker reporting a missing recipients list is normal for a two-party contract, and the report will explain this.

tool-drive-transfer.title: Drive Transfer: move data from one Google Drive to another, folders intact
tool-drive-transfer.note: Paste one Apps Script file into a Google Sheet on the new account, paste the old folder link, and Google copies the whole folder tree server-side. Nothing passes through your computer; the script keeps running round after round, logs every file and retries failures without duplicates.

sections.t: Switch Google accounts without downloading your whole Drive and uploading it again
sections.lead: The usual way is to download everything and upload it to the new account: slow, eats disk space, and a dropped connection means starting over. This tool lets Google copy from the old Drive to the new one on Google's own servers; you only paste two links.
ticks: Not a single byte through your computer
Folder tree kept, Google Docs/Sheets/Slides included
Keeps going until done, with a per-file log

sections.t: What it does for you

items.d: Uses Drive's server-side copy (makeCopy), so even multi-GB files never touch your home connection.
Subfolders are recreated in place, every file lands in the right folder, names unchanged.
Apps Script allows 6 minutes per run. The script stops at 4.5 minutes, schedules the next round and keeps going after you close the Sheet.
Each file gets an OK / LỖI (error) / BỎ QUA (skipped) row. A rescan only copies what is not in the log yet.

sections.t: Set up and run

items.d: Right-click the folder → Share → add the new account's email; Viewer is enough. To move a whole Drive, gather everything into one folder and share that.

items.t: Paste the script into a Sheet on the new account
items.d: Create a new Google Sheet → Extensions → Apps Script → delete the sample code, paste all of Code.gs (button below) → Save.

Reload the Sheet → Drive Transfer menu → Start a transfer… → authorize. Paste the source folder link and the destination link (leave empty to create one). Follow along in the log sheet or Show progress.
Filter the Status column by LỖI, fix the cause (missing access, storage full), then choose Rescan and copy missing files. Only delete the old account's data after checking.

sections.t: The first time you authorize, Google says "Google hasn't verified this app" because this is your own script running in your own account. Click Advanced → Go to … (unsafe). The script asks for Drive (read the source, create copies), the open Sheet (write the log), background triggers and sending email to yourself; it sends your data nowhere else.
Limits to know

items: One Apps Script run lasts at most 6 minutes; total trigger runtime is 90 minutes/day on personal Gmail and 6 hours/day on Google Workspace (Apps Script Quotas page). When the quota runs out the script retries and continues the next day.
Each user can upload and copy up to 750 GB per 24 hours (Google Workspace Help).
Copies are owned by the new account and count against its storage; originals are not deleted.
Comments, version history and old sharing settings do not carry over to the copies.

sections.t: FAQ

items.q: Can it transfer ownership instead of copying?
items.a: Between two personal Gmail accounts, Drive does not transfer ownership directly; the other side has to accept each file. Copying is what works in bulk; after checking, delete the originals in the old account.

items.q: What if I shut my computer down mid-run?
items.a: No problem. The script runs on Google's servers via triggers, so it keeps going after you close the Sheet or turn the computer off. Use Pause to stop it.

items.q: Will running it again create duplicates?
items.a: No. Successfully copied files are recorded in the log sheet by source ID; Rescan and copy missing files only copies what is missing, including failed files and files newly added to the source.

items.q: How do I move a different folder?
items.a: Choose Start a transfer… with another link. The old log is renamed with a timestamp and the new run writes to a fresh log sheet.

items.q: How long does it take?
items.a: It depends on the number of files more than their size, since each file is one copy call. I have not benchmarked it on a real Drive yet; watch files per round in Show progress to estimate.
